`audit-v1.jsonl` is a golden six-record audit session (schema v1, one chain, one checkpoint) generated by `crates/boxcar-audit/tests/golden.rs`; every verifier must accept it: `hash = blake3(prev_bytes || canonical_json(record without "hash"))`.
Go consumers must verify against it with a raw-number-preserving decoder (`json.Decoder.UseNumber`, or `json.RawMessage` per field): record 4 has `ts_host_ns` 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1), which a float64 cannot hold.
Canonical JSON is serde_json's compact output with keys sorted: only `"`, `\` and control characters are escaped, so `<>&` and U+2028 stay raw, while Go's `json.Marshal` escapes them and will not reproduce the hashes.

`control-v1.jsonl` is one example of each control protocol message (the hello, every op's request and response, every event, every error code, and the `--ready-fd` line), written by `cargo xtask schema` from the types in `crates/boxcar-proto/src/control.rs`; `crates/boxcar-proto/tests/control_golden.rs` checks that every line parses as what it is. The JSON Schemas of the control protocol, the audit records and the guest channel are in `../schema/`, from the same command. CI fails when either is out of date with the types.
